_comment: Copy to config.json and fill in the three paths. The real config.json is gitignored because it holds machine-specific absolute paths.
source_dir: <ABSOLUTE PATH TO THE FOLDER OF .czi FILES>
_section_order_note: Confirmed by user 2026-08-11. Serial order = scene index as acquired. The scanner ran column-major (s0 top-left, s1 below it, s2 next column top), and on staggered slides such as LS120_1a no grid model reproduces the physical layout at all.
_section_thickness_note: How thick the sections were cut. NOT recoverable from the CZIs - they carry no size_z, being single-plane images of a physical section - so it has to be supplied. This is the number the Abercrombie correction needs; see detection.abercrombie below. 14.0 for the LS dataset, operator-stated 2026-08-30.
_section_interval_note: Sections are CONSECUTIVE - the interval equals the thickness, operator-stated 2026-08-30. Two consequences. (1) section_order * 14 um is rostrocaudal position within the block, so the ~115 sections per animal are a ~1.6 mm forebrain block, which is consistent with every ROI in this study being telencephalic or preoptic. (2) Adjacent sections are NOT independent tissue: a nucleus cut by the boundary appears in both, so summing or averaging raw profile counts across neighbours double-counts it. That is exactly what the Abercrombie correction below removes, which is why it is enabled rather than optional here.

marker_identity._note: Filled in by 00c_channel_identity.py, then confirmed by the user. Until then neither fluorophore may be referred to as pERK or PCNA downstream.

flatfield._note: Per-pixel median across many randomly-positioned tiles, computed at reduced resolution because vignetting is low-frequency. BaSiC is the fallback if the tile-pitch power-spectrum test does not pass.

detection._note: Threshold is set once from the 03a calibration sweep, reviewed across more than one animal. With no negative control this is the most consequential parameter in the pipeline.

abercrombie._note: A single-plane image of a section counts nuclear PROFILES, not nuclei: a nucleus straddling the cut face still appears in the section it is cut into. Abercrombie N = n * T/(T + h), with T the section thickness and h the mean diameter of the counted object along the axis perpendicular to the section. At T=14 and h=7 the factor is 0.667 - uncorrected counts are 50% too high.
abercrombie._h_source: MEASURED per marker and region from the nuclear-counterstain segmentation, not taken from nucleus_diameter_um above. That value is a detection-scale assumption, and the factor moves from 0.737 to 0.583 across a plausible 5-10 um range, so using it would bury an unmeasured constant in every density.
abercrombie._what_it_does_not_fix: Abercrombie assumes spherical, randomly positioned objects and applies no lost-caps correction. The unbiased alternative is the optical or physical disector, which needs z-stacks a single-plane dataset does not have. Report raw and corrected counts side by side and say which is which.
abercrombie._effect_on_the_comparison: If h is similar between groups this is close to a constant multiplier, so it barely moves a between-group contrast. What it decides is whether a density can be quoted as cells per mm2 at all - a reporting fix, not a statistical one.

atlas_scope._note: Confirmed by user 2026-08-11. The atlas already labels Dm, Dl, Vv, Vs, Vd, Vc and POA. Add only the missing caudal social-behaviour-network nodes, using Wullimann 1996 and Nieuwenhuys 1982 as guides.
atlas_scope._regions_to_add_note: vTn = ventral tuberal nucleus, TPp = periventricular nucleus of posterior tuberculum (dopaminergic), PAG = periaqueductal / central grey.

blinding._note: No stage before 06b may read a group label. Outputs are keyed by animal ID only.
